# Independent audit of the coupled profile/residual exclusion

Source: `candidate 4dfc7dda63b85569`.

The actual middle maximum exists and is interior by the cited, already
audited finite-tilt theorem and the explicit zero-depth boundary argument.
Its critical continuous normals admit a positive circuit with at most
three members in the planar case. Their signed integer drift covers at
least one endpoint as well as the middle, and that covered endpoint has
volume at least the smaller endpoint a. The proof does not assume which
endpoint is covered. Two-cap circuits are excluded directly.

The finite saturation comparison gives U+V<=a for every actual critical
cap. In the strict case U+V<a both endpoint residuals are positive, so
their actual midpoint interpolation is legitimate. For fixed captured
sum, minimizing the concave residual-root sum at an endpoint and then
choosing the smaller whole fiber gives the asserted F_Q(q)<=0. If the
whole smaller endpoint is captured, q=Q-a is separated beforehand; no
empty residual is used as a Minkowski summand. The existence and monotonic
dependence of h(Q) are correct for d>=2 and the stated nonheavy regime.

The ordinary distal profile is used on each covered continuous convex
body separately. Its top-three form is coordinatewise increasing. This
justifies replacing covered endpoint masses by Q-q_i. The note explicitly
avoids the false minimum-entry monotonicity when the circuit has four or
more caps. For three caps the two profile inequalities eliminate to the
displayed expression with nonnegative coefficients.

For areas (1/4,1,121/100), the direct bound q_i<302/675 is especially
clean: a saturated small endpoint gives q_i<=89/300; all other rows have
positive residuals. The two justified squarings use positive quantities
and the exact surplus703/91125. The resulting strict bound, combined
with Q<=41/75, contradicts the exact equality in the profile inequality.
Thus the middle maximum is strictly ABOVE41/75, not merely unattained
at that value. Every point stays in the actual middle fiber and all
ambient halfspaces remain in the depth definition.

The homogeneity and measure checks are correct. No selection limit,
rounding, rational approximation, or shape assumption enters the theorem.
The effective ordinary cap-count refinement is correctly optional and
does not falsely impose three caps in higher dimension.
